name: root-pointer-vs-bindless

protocol.note: One load over a 4-byte allocation and one store to a separate 4-byte allocation, compiled through build_indexed_compute_package instead of build_linear_compute_package (ExecutionPlan::request_indexed_binding). Both distinct allocations collapse into one argument-buffer-style table binding (table_binding=0, stride=sizeof(uint64_t), count=2), dereferenced by the GPU through a real MTLBuffer.gpuAddress per-entry, in contrast to build_linear_compute_package's two separate buffer(N) slots for the identical IR (ADR-029).

correctness.oracle: reference::execute (build_linear_compute_package's ordinary load/store semantics -- the reference backend needs no indexed-specific code path, see ADR-029) plus compute_package.cpp's store_word_pattern byte-broadcast
correctness.tolerance: exact (report classification is an exact enum match; bytes must equal exactly 1; store's written bytes must exactly equal the byte-broadcast pattern of the stored value)

judgement: compiler::build_indexed_compute_package (ADR-029) gives E007 a real Metal + reference result under a genuine Direct lowering -- the opposite classification choice from ADR-028's E002 CachedObject lowering, because this experiment specifically measures the cost of a table the GPU actually dereferences at runtime, not a host-resolved binding. The compiled report's compute_package event reports bytes=1 (one table binding) in direct contrast to the linear path's N separate buffer(N) slots for the same two-allocation IR -- exactly the N-vs-1 binding-count signal this experiment is named for. Getting a real result required bypassing a known-stale CapabilitySnapshot::gpu_addresses bit (hardcoded false, never wired to a real check, discovered in a prior milestone and left unfixed) with a narrowly-scoped Impl::probe_gpu_addresses() runtime check instead -- this machine's Metal device was confirmed via vertical-slice.metal.indexed-binding to genuinely support MTLBuffer.gpuAddress, so the test exercises the real dispatch path, not the honest-Unsupported-skip fallback. The residency cost (every referenced allocation still requires a useResource: call even though only the table occupies a binding slot) is reported honestly in ADR-029's prose rather than folded into the bytes metric, keeping the binding-count contrast legible. Reference backend required zero code changes: it never reads request_indexed_binding or branches on indexed_compute_package at all, since build_indexed_compute_package's IR contract is a strict subset of what the ordinary linear path already executes correctly.
vulkan_status: compile-review-only (ADR-024); vulkan_device_hal.cpp still calls build_linear_compute_package unconditionally and never branches on request_indexed_binding -- a documentation-only comment block above DeviceHal::compile maps the hypothetical VgIndexedPushConstants table array (reusing E002/ADR-028's VgAllocationRef buffer_reference convention) onto this backend, with zero functional change. Real descriptor indexing (VK_EXT_descriptor_indexing/nonuniformEXT) as the traditional bindless comparison baseline is explicitly out of scope -- this backend has no descriptor-set/pool infrastructure at all, and building that subsystem for a compile-review-only requirement would be disproportionate; this is the largest single scope deferral in the whole Phase B gate plan (ADR-029).
